pr_title: Cleanup SetResourceInstanceCurrent to be clearer and more reliable
pr_body:
Refactors `setResourceInstanceCurrent` which does lots of things, to do them in a more reliable and predictable order. Deletes dead code in eval_diff discovered over the course of investigation, following our "clean it up if you're nearby" practice.

- Fixes https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/issues/23077
- Fixes https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/issues/23026
- Fixes https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform/issues/23419
pr_comments:
Some of the test failures are typical, they were written to expect the wrong output.

The problematic ones are where we have the wrong provider stored in the state. I don't think this change is at fault for that however, and I bet it's highlighting that we don't update the provider consistently throughout the lifecycle of the resource.
@jbardin disagree, I think this change is at fault ... ~I added a line (where we call `setMeta...` _again_ ...) that fixes them.~ Actually, changed it since it's only the provider update.

yeah, It could just be because the function is overloaded, but the fact that the _wrong_ providers were in there make me wonder if it's not set consistently, and only cleaned up "just in time". (your last fix is still good, we want to restore everything this function needs to do for now)
@apparentlymart Very very helpful catch, found and fixed.

I'm going to lock this issue because it has been closed for _30 days_ ⏳. This helps our maintainers find and focus on the active issues.

If you have found a problem that seems similar to this, please open a new issue and complete the issue template so we can capture all the details necessary to investigate further.

issue_context.title: for_each referencing errors
issue_context.body:
### Terraform Version

```
Terraform v0.12.10 (also reproducible with v0.12.9)
+ provider.azuread v0.6.0
+ provider.azurerm v1.34.0
+ provider.external v1.2.0
+ provider.null v2.1.2
+ provider.random v2.2.1
```

### Terraform Configuration Files
**storage.tf**
```
resource "azurerm_storage_account" "edp" {
  for_each                  = toset(var.storage_account_types)
  name                      = "${lower(var.storage_account_name)}${each.value}"
  resource_group_name       = var.resource_group_name
  location                  = var.location
  account_tier              = "Standard"
  account_kind              = "StorageV2"
  account_replication_type  = each.value == "global" ? "GRS" : "LRS"
  enable_https_traffic_only = true
  enable_blob_encryption    = true
  enable_file_encryption    = true
  enable_advanced_threat_protection = true

  tags = merge(var.tags, { purpose = each.value })

  identity {
    type = "SystemAssigned"
  }

  lifecycle {
    ignore_changes = [account_encryption_source]
  }

  network_rules {
    bypass = var.network_bypass

    default_action = var.network_default_action

    # Storage account firewall won't take a /32 CIDR
    ip_rules = [for i in var.network_ip_rules : split("/32", i)[0]]

    virtual_network_subnet_ids = var.network_subnet_ids
  }
}

data "azurerm_key_vault" "storage" {
  name                = var.encryption_key_vault_name
  resource_group_name = var.encryption_resource_group_name
}

data "azurerm_key_vault_key" "hsm" {
  name         = var.encryption_key_name
  key_vault_id = data.azurerm_key_vault.storage.id
}

resource "azurerm_key_vault_access_policy" "storage" {
  for_each = toset(var.storage_account_types)
  key_vault_id = data.azurerm_key_vault.storage.id

  tenant_id = azurerm_storage_account.edp[each.value].identity[0].tenant_id
  object_id = azurerm_storage_account.edp[each.value].identity[0].principal_id
...
```
**variables.tf**
```
...
variable "storage_account_types" {
  type        = list(string)
  description = "The flavors of storage accounts for tenants"
  default     = ["raw", "global", "apps"]
}
...
```

### Expected Behavior
Terraform should be able to reference the elements correctly. 

### Steps to Reproduce

1. `terraform init`
2. `terraform apply`

### Additional Context
When looking at the referenced issues (see below), it appears that this problem was fixed in Terraform v0.12.7. 
I can confirm it works correctly in  v0.12.7, however It seems the issue has been reintroduced in v0.12.9 and v0.12.10 (not sure about v0.12.8).

review_comments:
A further thought here, after some additional pondering:

I wonder if perhaps the situation we were trying to allow for here was the evaluation of the dependent expression (`test.a.*.id` in the above example) during the _plan_ phase. Testing for that in _automated_ testing is likely to be fiddly (though possible, I think) but perhaps a quick _manual_ test would be to work with the configuration I described above but look closely at the `terraform plan` output on the second plan (when `a_count` is set to zero for the first time).

Ideally we'd want to see something like this:

```hcl
    ~ foo: [
        - "some-id-1",
        - "some-id-2",
      ]
```

...but I worry we might see something like this instead:

```hcl
    ~ foo: [
          "some-id-1",
          "some-id-2",
      ] -> (known after apply)
```

It being briefly unknown isn't a big deal in this example, but the difference between that being known-empty or unknown can be important if there are any expressions deriving in turn from `test.a.foo`, which could make this a breaking change.

---

I wrote the above example originally thinking about it going in a context test with a mocked provider that could provide that `foo` argument, but to test it in a manual testing situation would require using a "real" provider. Hopefully that example translates okay to using `null_resource`, though since null resource `triggers` only accepts strings it'll require some additional complexity I suppose:

```hcl
  triggers = {
    foo = join(",", null_resource.a.*.id)
  }
```

This'll mean that the "good" diff would be from a non-empty string to an empty string, rather than a non-empty list to an empty list, but a similar principle should apply.

Thanks for these! The manual testing did indeed confirm this is an issue ... `master` puts a reference error (as it should) but this branch does not. Will keep re-reading these comments and try and develop some understanding.

One thing I'm going to need to read (I did a bunch of poking at the manual test before reading rest of the comment and the second comment) is understanding why evaluate is thinking differently about `nil` resources.

Presently, what happens on the branch is that it will go through `plan` but then there are unknown values during apply. The reference issue should be caught during plan, so that's what I'm trying to run down.

Got it, I think. That the NoEach check can happen in this function, so that we don't delete the resource early (I added a similar comment to what you wrote, that we allow resources with 0 instances to continue to exist if they're a Map or List). Now to wait for the tests to come back 🙃

I think this comment is now not totally accurate, because we can get here in the case where the resource exists but has _no_ other instances. The code around it seems correct, but since you've gone to the effort of adding all of these great comments I thought you'd probably want to clarify this one. :grinning:
